# Discord announcement (Saturday AM) — generated by pavel-voice, variant 2 of 2, unedited

Hey all,

I've just hacked Fittest overnight using NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit 0.3.0-rc.
There are 2 things you can use now:

1) DisagreementHook
You can simply drop this into any in-flight ALCHEMI run with any set of models and it will automatically route structures where the models disagree to your DFT / oracle queue.

2) A simple trust service
Just send the structures and it returns for each structure the overall trust score as well as the trusted model (or average of models) you should use to evaluate the reaction.

Some results on held-out Transition1x reactions:
- Disagreement between MACE-MPA-0, AIMNet2 and Orb flags where AIMNet2 is wrong: AUROC 0.92
- AIMNet2's own 4-member seed ensemble on these reactions: AUROC 0.80

Seed ensembles are unfortunately overconfident, as their ensemble spread is ~0.4x the real error.

The repo is here: https://github.com/Pavel-Tk/fittest
It's under MIT license.
To reproduce the results please see the instructions in the repo: docs/REPRODUCE.md

If you are doing MLIPs, you can just plug your model as an agent (it's just a small backend class) or send me structures and I can run them for you.

Come find me if you have questions!

voice: pavel-v1-gemma4 · gemma-4-E4B-it + pavel LoRA (SFT epoch 2 + anti-AI DPO) · Q6_K + f16 LoRA

---
Fact-check notes (lead): 0.92 = arm C committee σ AUROC vs "AIMNet2 wrong" (force RMSE > 0.25 eV/Å) on the leak-free eval split; 0.80 = AIMNet2 4-member ensemble on the same target; 0.4× = per-frame median spread/error of the AIMNet2 ensemble on all 3,157 T1x test frames. Variant 1 was rejected because it invented "send the structures via the website".

# Discord update: the live MCP server (Saturday PM) — generated by pavel-voice, variant 1 of 2, unedited

Hey everyone. Just wanted to update my previous post:
TrustSwarm is now called Fittest.

The swarm of ML interatomic potentials (MACE-MPA-0, AIMNet2, Orb-v3) that I was developing is now live as a public MCP server that anyone can call: https://fittest-mcp.westus2.cloudapp.azure.com/mcp

You can add it to Claude Code in one line:
claude mcp add --transport http fittest https://fittest-mcp.westus2.cloudapp.azure.com/mcp

It also works in Claude Desktop and Cursor (setup on the landing page: https://fittest-mcp.westus2.cloudapp.azure.com/)

How to use it:
1) Send a molecule in XYZ format
2) It will output which model (or blend of models) to trust, a trust score for that model / blend, or "send this one to DFT" if the models disagree
3) The system is calibrated on C/H/N/O reaction chemistry from Transition1x. If you send molecules outside of this scope, it will output a warning

The system anonymously logs each call (what tool was called, timings, counts), but does not store any structures.

Please try it out with your molecules & tell me where it breaks.
The repo is here: https://github.com/Pavel-Tk/fittest (MIT)

voice: pavel-v1-gemma4 · gemma-4-E4B-it + pavel LoRA (SFT epoch 2 + anti-AI DPO) · Q6_K + f16 LoRA

---
Fact-check notes (lead): every fact matches docs/MCP.md. Variant 2 was rejected: it said "trust score out of 100" (the score is 0–1) and that out-of-domain molecules get "a warning instead of a recommendation" (they get both).

# Discord post v3: use case first (Saturday PM, replaces the update above) — pavel-voice, variant 1 of 3 (second round), unedited

Hey folks,
If you are doing ML interatomic potentials for molecules / reactions, now you can also ask the model to decide if it should trust the result or send to DFT.
For each molecule you will get:
- Which model to use (MACE-MPA-0, AIMNet2, Orb-v3)
- A trust score
- Flag to send to DFT if models disagree
This way you can use your limited budget on DFT only where needed, and avoid silent failures (e.g. at transition states).
On held out Transition1x reactions it showed 28% lower force error than the best baseline & trusted none of the 96 badly wrong answers.
I've built this during this hackathon, it's called Fittest
You can try it:
In Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http fittest https://fittest-mcp.westus2.cloudapp.azure.com/mcp`
On Claude Desktop / Cursor: https://fittest-mcp.westus2.cloudapp.azure.com/

It is calibrated on C/H/N/O reaction chemistry and warns you if you are outside of this.
Privacy: yes, we log anonymously all info about the calls (which tool was called, the counts, timing) and no molecules themselves are stored.

Send me your molecules & tell me where it breaks 
https://github.com/Pavel-Tk/fittest

voice: pavel-v1-gemma4 · gemma-4-E4B-it + pavel LoRA (SFT epoch 2 + anti-AI DPO) · Q6_K + f16 LoRA
